claim_text_en: Volunteers matched the length of a line to one of three comparison lines — a task so clear that, judging alone, control participants were accurate on over 99% of estimates, while the scripted majority's wrong answers were off by three quarters of an inch to an inch and three quarters. Seated in a group whose other members had secretly agreed to give the same wrong answer on 12 of 18 trials, the 123 participants in the core experiments moved to the majority's wrong answer on 36.8% of those critical judgments.
claim_text_pl: Ochotnicy dopasowywali długość linii do jednej z trzech linii porównawczych — zadanie było tak jednoznaczne, że oceniając w pojedynkę, uczestnicy z grupy kontrolnej trafiali w ponad 99% ocen, podczas gdy błędne odpowiedzi zaaranżowanej większości mijały się z prawdą o trzy czwarte cala do cala i trzech czwartych. Posadzeni w grupie, której pozostali członkowie potajemnie umówili się podawać tę samą błędną odpowiedź w 12 z 18 prób, 123 uczestnicy głównych eksperymentów przechodzili na błędną odpowiedź większości w 36,8% tych krytycznych ocen.
support_notes_en: asch-1956-monograph: Read directly from the scanned monograph: control estimates 'showed an accuracy of over 99 per cent' (p. 3); the majority's estimates 'departed from the true value by amounts ranging from 3/4 to 1 3/4 inches' (p. 3, Table 1); 12 critical trials among 18 comparisons (pp. 6-7); Table 3 (p. 10) gives N=123 across three experimental groups, mean per cent errors 36.8, against 0.7 per cent in the control group (N=37). | asch-1951-group-pressure: The program's first report confirms the structure: a group of eight with one naive critical subject, unanimous wrong answers on 12 of 18 trials (Table 1), mean 3.84 errors against 0.08 in controls (Table 2), and one-third of critical-group estimates displaced toward the majority; its text describes the majority's errors as ranging between 1/2 and 1 3/4 inches.

claim_text_en: Participants were recruited for what appeared to be a simple experiment in visual discrimination; the prearrangement with the majority was hidden. Asch ended every session with an individual interview in which the purpose of the experiment, the participant's role and the majority's role were fully explained — he considered it neither advisable nor justified to let anyone leave without that explanation.
claim_text_pl: Uczestników rekrutowano na coś, co wyglądało na prosty eksperyment nad rozróżnianiem wzrokowym; wcześniejsza umowa z większością była przed nimi ukryta. Asch kończył każdą sesję indywidualną rozmową, w której w pełni wyjaśniał cel eksperymentu, rolę uczestnika i rolę większości — uważał, że pozwolenie komukolwiek wyjść bez tego wyjaśnienia nie byłoby ani wskazane, ani uzasadnione.
support_notes_en: asch-1956-monograph: P. 3: subjects gathered 'to take part in what appeared to be a simple experiment in visual discrimination' and the critical subject 'was not aware of this prearrangement'; p. 9: an individual interview 'followed immediately upon the conclusion of the experiment', 'the purport of the experiment was explained in full', and 'We did not consider it advisable or justified to allow subjects to leave without receiving an explanation of the procedure and the reasons for the investigation.' | asch-1951-group-pressure: P. 225 of the reprint: 'Toward the conclusion of the interview each subject was informed fully of the purpose of the experiment, of his role and of that of the majority', with the surrounding passage stating the experimenter's responsibility to clarify doubts and explain why the subject was placed in the situation.

claim_text_en: Unanimity mattered more than numbers. A single fellow dissenter cut pro-majority errors from 32% to about 10% (5.5% when the partner was instructed to answer accurately), and Asch reported that a unanimous majority of three was far more effective than a majority of eight containing one dissenter — while majorities larger than three added almost nothing to the pressure.
claim_text_pl: Jednomyślność znaczyła więcej niż liczebność. Jedna osoba sprzeciwiająca się razem z uczestnikiem obniżała błędy po stronie większości z 32% do około 10% (5,5%, gdy partner miał polecenie odpowiadać zgodnie z prawdą), a Asch podawał, że jednomyślna większość trzech osób była znacznie skuteczniejsza niż ośmioosobowa większość, w której jedna osoba się wyłamywała — podczas gdy większości liczniejsze niż trzy osoby prawie nic już do presji nie dodawały.
support_notes_en: asch-1951-group-pressure: Reports pro-majority errors dropping to 10.4 per cent with a second naive subject and 5.5 per cent with an instructed accurate partner, against 32 per cent under the unanimous baseline; states 'a unanimous majority of three is, under the given conditions, far more effective than a majority of eight containing one dissenter'; and Table 3 with the surrounding text: 'The effect appeared in full force with a majority of three. Larger majorities of four, eight, and sixteen did not produce effects greater than a majority of three.' | asch-1955-sciam: Corroborates both series for the larger sample: with a supporting partner present, subjects 'answered incorrectly only one fourth as often as under the pressure of a unanimous majority'; against two opponents errors were 13.6 per cent and against three 31.8 per cent, while a single opponent swayed subjects little.

claim_text_en: The average hides the range: about one quarter of participants (24%) never once went with the majority, roughly as many (27%) went with it on eight or more of the twelve critical trials, and the rest fell in between — Asch himself counted the wide individual differences among the study's significant findings.
claim_text_pl: Średnia ukrywa rozrzut: około jedna czwarta uczestników (24%) ani razu nie poszła za większością, mniej więcej tyle samo osób (27%) poszło za nią w ośmiu lub więcej z dwunastu prób krytycznych, a reszta znalazła się pośrodku — sam Asch zaliczał te duże różnice indywidualne do istotnych ustaleń badania.
support_notes_en: asch-1956-monograph: P. 11: 'One-fourth of the experimental groups (24 per cent) gave errorless estimates, while an approximately equal number (27 per cent) gave majority-determined estimates from eight to twelve times. Between these extremes is to be found one-half of the critical group'; and 'That the majority elicited widely different reactions is one significant aspect of the present findings.' | asch-1955-sciam: States that about one quarter of the subjects were completely independent and never agreed with the erroneous judgments of the majority, while at the other extreme some individuals went with the majority nearly all the time.

claim_text_en: Most of what happened in Asch's laboratory was not conformity: across the core experiments about two thirds of all critical judgments were correct despite the pressure, and Asch read his results as much as a study of independence as of yielding. A content analysis of 99 social psychology textbook accounts published between 1953 and 1984 found that authors increasingly accentuated the role of conformity and underestimated that of independence.
claim_text_pl: Większość tego, co działo się w laboratorium Ascha, nie była konformizmem: w głównych eksperymentach około dwóch trzecich wszystkich krytycznych ocen było mimo presji poprawnych, a Asch odczytywał swoje wyniki w równym stopniu jako badanie niezależności, co ulegania. Analiza treści 99 podręcznikowych omówień z psychologii społecznej opublikowanych w latach 1953–1984 wykazała, że autorzy coraz mocniej podkreślali rolę konformizmu, a nie doceniali roli niezależności.
support_notes_en: friend-rafferty-bramel-1990: Official abstract (read via Crossref metadata): Asch 'equally, if not more, intended and interpreted it as demonstrating the powers of independence'; the evidence is '99 accounts in social psychology textbooks published between 1953 ... and 1984'; the authors found accounts 'have increasingly accentuated the role of conformity and underestimated that of independence'. | asch-1956-monograph: Table 3 (p. 10): mean per cent errors 36.8 for all experimental groups, i.e. about 63 per cent of critical estimates correct; p. 10 states 'the preponderance of estimates was, in each of the experimental groups, correct or independent of the majority'. The 1951 report gives 68 per cent correct for its 50 subjects, so 'about two thirds' covers both reports.

claim_text_en: The size of the effect is not a constant of human nature: a meta-analysis of 133 Asch-type studies from 17 countries found that conformity in US studies had declined since the 1950s, and that collectivist countries tended to show higher levels of conformity than individualist ones — with the cultural measures mattering more than classic situational moderators such as majority size.
claim_text_pl: Wielkość tego efektu nie jest stałą ludzkiej natury: metaanaliza 133 badań typu Ascha z 17 krajów wykazała, że konformizm w badaniach amerykańskich malał od lat pięćdziesiątych, a kraje kolektywistyczne zwykle wykazywały wyższy poziom konformizmu niż indywidualistyczne — przy czym miary kulturowe ważyły więcej niż klasyczne moderatory sytuacyjne, takie jak liczebność większości.
support_notes_en: bond-smith-1996: Official abstract: 'The literature search produced 133 studies drawn from 17 countries. An analysis of US studies found that conformity has declined since the 1950s. ... Collectivist countries tended to show higher levels of conformity than individualist countries.' Abstract-level access only; effect sizes and moderator tables were not read. | capuano-chekroun-2024: Open-access systematic review summarizing Bond and Smith (1996): 'conformity appears to be higher in collectivist cultures than in so-called individualist cultures. More importantly, the impact of these cultural values was greater than other situational variables considered key moderators, such as majority size' — the source for the 'mattering more than majority size' clause.

claim_text_en: The basic effect still replicates: a 2024 systematic review of conformity research reports recent Asch-type studies finding rates close to the originals, including a 2023 replication with a conformity rate of 33%.
claim_text_pl: Podstawowy efekt wciąż się replikuje: pochodzący z 2024 roku przegląd systematyczny badań nad konformizmem odnotowuje niedawne badania typu Ascha ze wskaźnikami bliskimi oryginalnym, w tym replikację z 2023 roku ze wskaźnikiem konformizmu 33%.
support_notes_en: capuano-chekroun-2024: States that 'recent investigations have indeed reported conformity rates closely resembling those observed by Asch in the 1950s, exemplified by the replication conducted by Franzen and Mader (2023), which observed a conformity rate of 33%, mirroring Asch's rates'. The Franzen and Mader paper itself was not opened; the claim is attributed to the review.

claim_text_en: John Searle asks you to imagine him locked in a room with a batch of Chinese writing, which to him is so many meaningless squiggles, together with rulebooks in English for matching one batch of symbols to another purely by their shapes. Slips of paper come in, he consults the rules, he passes symbols back out. Unknown to him, the people outside call the batches the script, the story and the questions, call what he hands back the answers, and call the rulebooks the program. He gets good enough that his Chinese answers are indistinguishable from a native speaker's — and he still does not understand a word of Chinese.
claim_text_pl: John Searle prosi, żebyś wyobraził go sobie zamkniętego w pokoju z zestawem chińskich napisów, które są dla niego tylko stertą bezsensownych zawijasów, oraz z angielskimi księgami reguł pozwalającymi dopasowywać jeden zestaw symboli do drugiego wyłącznie po ich kształtach. Do środka trafiają kartki, on sprawdza reguły i wypuszcza symbole z powrotem na zewnątrz. Nie wie o tym, ale ludzie na zewnątrz nazywają kolejne zestawy skryptem, opowiadaniem i pytaniami, to, co im oddaje, nazywają odpowiedziami, a księgi reguł — programem. Dochodzi w tym do takiej wprawy, że jego chińskie odpowiedzi są nie do odróżnienia od odpowiedzi rodzimego użytkownika chińskiego — a on wciąż nie rozumie ani słowa po chińsku.
support_notes_en: searle-1980: Full text read. Searle sets up the Gedankenexperiment as being "locked in a room and given a large batch of Chinese writing" which is "just so many meaningless squiggles"; the second and third batches come with English rules for correlating symbols "entirely by their shapes"; he records that the people outside "call the first batch 'a script'", the second "a story", the third "questions", his output "answers to the questions", and the English rules "the program"; and that his answers become "absolutely indistinguishable from those of native Chinese speakers" while "I do not understand a word of the Chinese stories."

claim_text_en: Searle is careful about the target. He distinguishes weak AI — the computer as a powerful tool for formulating and testing hypotheses about the mind, to which he says he has no objection — from strong AI, the claim that an appropriately programmed computer really is a mind, can literally be said to understand, and that the programs are themselves the explanations of human cognition. Only the second is under attack, and the attack is not the claim that machines cannot think: he writes that he sees no reason in principle why a machine could not be given the capacity to understand Chinese, since our bodies with our brains are precisely such machines.
claim_text_pl: Searle starannie wybiera cel. Odróżnia słabą sztuczną inteligencję — komputer jako potężne narzędzie do formułowania i sprawdzania hipotez o umyśle, wobec której, jak pisze, nie ma żadnych zastrzeżeń — od mocnej sztucznej inteligencji, czyli tezy, że odpowiednio zaprogramowany komputer naprawdę jest umysłem, że dosłownie można o nim powiedzieć, iż rozumie, i że same programy są wyjaśnieniami ludzkiego poznania. Atak wymierzony jest wyłącznie w to drugie i nie jest twierdzeniem, że maszyny nie mogą myśleć: Searle pisze, że nie widzi zasadniczego powodu, dla którego nie można by wyposażyć maszyny w zdolność rozumienia chińskiego, skoro nasze ciała wraz z mózgami są dokładnie takimi maszynami.
support_notes_en: searle-1980: Full text read. Weak AI is defined as the view that "the principal value of the computer in the study of the mind is that it gives us a very powerful tool"; strong AI as the view that "the appropriately programmed computer really is a mind" and that "the programs are themselves the explanations". Searle writes "I have no objection to the claims of weak AI", and later "I see no reason in principle why we couldn't give a machine the capacity to understand English or Chinese, since in an important sense our bodies with our brains are precisely such machines."

claim_text_en: What the room is meant to establish is a gap that no amount of programming closes. Formal symbol manipulations by themselves carry no intentionality, Searle argues, because the symbols are identified entirely by their shapes: in his phrase they have only a syntax but no semantics, and such intentionality as computers appear to have lies in the minds of those who program them and those who read their output. The positive half of his position is the mirror image — mental states are literally a product of the operation of the brain, so any mechanism capable of producing intentionality must have causal powers at least equal to those of brains, which he treats as an empirical question rather than a programming one.
claim_text_pl: To, co pokój ma wykazać, to luka, której nie domknie żadna ilość programowania. Same formalne manipulacje symbolami nie niosą żadnej intencjonalności — dowodzi Searle — ponieważ symbole są identyfikowane wyłącznie po kształtach: w jego sformułowaniu mają tylko składnię, ale nie mają semantyki, a taka intencjonalność, jaką komputery zdają się mieć, mieszka w umysłach tych, którzy je programują, i tych, którzy odczytują ich wyniki. Pozytywna połowa jego stanowiska jest lustrzanym odbiciem tamtej: stany mentalne są dosłownie produktem działania mózgu, więc każdy mechanizm zdolny wytwarzać intencjonalność musi mieć moce przyczynowe co najmniej równe mocom mózgów — a to Searle traktuje jako kwestię empiryczną, a nie kwestię programowania.
support_notes_en: searle-1980: Full text read. "Because the formal symbol manipulations by themselves don't have any intentionality ... In the linguistic jargon, they have only a syntax but no semantics. Such intentionality as computers appear to have is solely in the minds of those who program them and those who use them." The abstract states the positive half: intentionality "is a product of causal features of the brain" and "Any mechanism capable of producing intentionality must have causal powers equal to those of the brain"; whether some other chemistry could do it is called "an empirical question, rather like the question whether photosynthesis can be done by something with a chemistry different from that of chlorophyll."

claim_text_en: To the systems reply — the man does not understand, but the whole system of man plus rulebooks plus scratch paper does — Searle answers: let him memorise the rules and the data banks and do the calculations in his head, then work outdoors with no room at all; there is now nothing in the system that is not in him, and he still understands nothing. To the robot reply — put the computer inside a body with a television camera and arms — he answers that the extra input arrives as more uninterpreted symbols, so he would be the robot's homunculus without knowing what any of it was about. To the brain simulator reply — model the sequence of neuron firings in a Chinese speaker's brain — he substitutes a man operating an elaborate set of water pipes and valves, and says the simulation reproduces the wrong properties: the formal structure of the firings rather than the causal powers that do the work.
claim_text_pl: Na odpowiedź systemową — człowiek nie rozumie, ale rozumie cały system: człowiek plus księgi reguł plus kartki na brudno — Searle odpowiada: niech nauczy się na pamięć reguł i banków danych, a obliczenia niech wykonuje w głowie, a potem niech pracuje pod gołym niebem, bez żadnego pokoju; teraz w systemie nie ma już niczego, czego nie byłoby w nim samym, a on nadal nic nie rozumie. Na odpowiedź robotyczną — umieśćmy komputer w ciele z kamerą telewizyjną i ramionami — odpowiada, że dodatkowe dane wejściowe przychodzą jako kolejne nieinterpretowane symbole, więc byłby homunkulusem robota, nie wiedząc, o co w tym wszystkim chodzi. Na odpowiedź symulatora mózgu — zamodelujmy sekwencję wyładowań neuronów w mózgu osoby mówiącej po chińsku — podstawia człowieka obsługującego rozbudowany układ rur i zaworów wodnych i mówi, że symulacja odtwarza niewłaściwe własności: formalną strukturę wyładowań, a nie moce przyczynowe, które wykonują właściwą pracę.
support_notes_en: searle-1980: Full text read, replies I-III. Systems reply (attributed to Berkeley): "let the individual internalize all of these elements of the system. He memorizes the rules in the ledger and the data banks of Chinese symbols ... We can even get rid of the room and suppose he works outdoors ... there isn't anything in the system that isn't in him." Robot reply (Yale): the camera output is Chinese symbols he manipulates without knowing what they mean — "I am the robot's homunculus, but unlike the traditional homunculus, I don't know what's going on." Brain simulator reply (Berkeley and M.I.T.): the water-pipes-and-valves version, of which he writes "it is simulating the wrong things about the brain ... it won't have simulated what matters about the brain, namely its causal properties." | sep-chinese-room: Read via the live entry (substantive revision 23 October 2024); the passages used here were checked against the downloaded HTML. Sets out the same three replies and Searle's counters, and names the philosophers who have defended each — Block, Copeland, Dennett, Hofstadter, Fodor, Haugeland, Kurzweil and Rey for the systems reply; Boden, Crane, Dennett, Fodor, Harnad, Moravec and Rey for the robot reply — which is the basis for describing the counters as contested rather than conclusive.

claim_text_en: Paul and Patricia Churchland, writing in Scientific American in 1990, agreed with Searle that the room does not understand Chinese and rejected his argument anyway. Their target is his third axiom — that syntax by itself is neither constitutive of nor sufficient for semantics — which they say is already carrying ninety percent of the weight of the conclusion and which they read as begging the question against the research programme it is aimed at. Their parody is a luminous room: a man pumps a bar magnet up and down, no light appears, and one concludes that forces are neither constitutive of nor sufficient for luminance — an inference that would have felt just as intuitive, and been just as wrong, against Maxwell in the 1860s.
claim_text_pl: Paul i Patricia Churchlandowie, piszący w 1990 roku na łamach Scientific American, zgodzili się z Searle'em, że pokój nie rozumie chińskiego, i mimo to odrzucili jego argument. Ich celem jest jego trzeci aksjomat — że sama składnia ani nie konstytuuje semantyki, ani do niej nie wystarcza — o którym mówią, że niesie już dziewięćdziesiąt procent ciężaru wniosku, i który czytają jako z góry przesądzający spór z programem badawczym, przeciw któremu jest wymierzony. Ich parodią jest świetlisty pokój: człowiek pompuje w górę i w dół magnesem sztabkowym, żadne światło się nie pojawia i wyciąga się wniosek, że siły ani nie konstytuują świetlistości, ani do niej nie wystarczają — wnioskowanie, które wytoczone przeciw Maxwellowi w latach sześćdziesiątych XIX wieku wydawałoby się dokładnie tak samo intuicyjne i byłoby dokładnie tak samo błędne.
support_notes_en: churchland-churchland-1990: Pages 32-36 read from a JSTOR scan on Patricia Churchland's own site. "We agree with Searle that the Chinese room does not understand Chinese" but reject the argument because axiom 3 — printed in their box as "Syntax by itself is neither constitutive of nor sufficient for semantics" — is "tantamount to begging the question against the research program of classical AI", and "Plainly, his third axiom is already carrying 90 percent of the weight of this almost identical conclusion." The luminous room is their parallel: a man pumping a bar magnet in a dark room produces "no luminance at all", yielding the axioms "Electricity and magnetism are forces", "The essential property of light is luminance", "Forces by themselves are neither constitutive of nor sufficient for luminance" and the conclusion that electricity and magnetism are neither constitutive of nor sufficient for light — offered as a transparently fallacious parallel raised shortly after Maxwell's 1864 suggestion.

claim_text_en: The dispute was staged from the start. Behavioral and Brain Sciences ran the target article alongside comments and criticisms from twenty-seven cognitive science researchers, followed by Searle's replies to them, and that response argues by name with Ned Block, Daniel Dennett, Zenon Pylyshyn, Jerry Fodor, Marvin Minsky, John Haugeland, Richard Rorty, John McCarthy, Roger Schank and Robert Wilensky. Dennett's line that he understands English but his brain does not draws the retort that this is as implausible as insisting one digests pizza while one's stomach does not.
claim_text_pl: Spór był wyreżyserowany od samego początku. Behavioral and Brain Sciences opublikowało artykuł główny razem z komentarzami i krytykami dwudziestu siedmiu badaczy kognitywistyki, a po nich odpowiedź Searle'a na te głosy, która polemizuje imiennie z Nedem Blockiem, Danielem Dennettem, Zenonem Pylyshynem, Jerrym Fodorem, Marvinem Minskym, Johnem Haugelandem, Richardem Rortym, Johnem McCarthym, Rogerem Schankiem i Robertem Wilenskym. Zdanie Dennetta, że rozumie angielski, ale jego mózg nie, ściąga na siebie ripostę, że jest to równie nieprawdopodobne jak upieranie się, że ktoś trawi pizzę, a jego żołądek nie.
support_notes_en: searle-1980-bbs-commentary: Scanned pages 437-439 and 450-453 of the printed BBS issue read. The Author's Response, "Intrinsic intentionality", is headed by Searle's remark that he is "pleased at the amount of interest my target article has aroused" and works through named commentators — Block, Dennett, Pylyshyn, Marshall, Wilensky, Minsky, Fodor, Haugeland, Rorty, McCarthy, Schank, Abelson, Sloman & Croucher, Lycan, Bridgeman. On Dennett: 'He says "I understand English but my brain doesn't." ... I find his claim as implausible as insisting, "I digest pizza; my stomach and digestive tract don't."' Commentaries by Grover Maxwell, E. W. Menzel Jr. and Marvin Minsky are visible in full on the pages read. | sep-chinese-room: States that "Searle's article in BBS was published along with comments and criticisms by 27 cognitive science researchers" and that "These 27 comments were followed by Searle's replies to his critics" — the source of the count, which the partial scan read here cannot establish on its own.

claim_text_en: Four decades on, the field has not converged. The journal's own editor, Stevan Harnad, records that the overwhelming majority still think the Chinese Room argument is dead wrong, and the sheer volume of refutations prompted Pat Hayes to suggest that cognitive science be redefined as the ongoing research program of showing it to be false; Dennett calls it a misleading intuition pump that depends on getting you to imagine too simple a case. Philosophers remain divided between the systems and virtual-mind camps and those who defend Searle's conclusion, and recent advances in large language models have not resolved the debate.
claim_text_pl: Cztery dekady później dziedzina nadal nie doszła do wspólnego stanowiska. Stevan Harnad, redaktor tego właśnie czasopisma, odnotowuje, że przytłaczająca większość wciąż uważa argument chińskiego pokoju za kompletnie błędny, a sama liczba refutacji skłoniła Pata Hayesa do propozycji, by kognitywistykę przedefiniować jako trwający program badawczy wykazywania, że argument ten jest fałszywy; Dennett nazywa go mylącą „pompą intuicji” (*intuition pump*), która opiera się na skłonieniu cię do wyobrażenia sobie zbyt prostego przypadku. Filozofowie pozostają podzieleni między obozami odpowiedzi systemowej i wirtualnego umysłu a obrońcami wniosku Searle'a, a niedawne postępy w dużych modelach językowych nie rozstrzygnęły tego sporu.
support_notes_en: wikipedia-chinese-room: Raw article source downloaded and searched directly; the passages quoted here were read in it. Records that BBS editor Stevan Harnad notes "The overwhelming majority ... still think that the Chinese Room Argument is dead wrong" (citing Harnad 2001), that the literature "inspired Pat Hayes to comment that the field of cognitive science ought to be redefined as 'the ongoing research program of showing Searle's Chinese Room Argument to be false'", and that Dennett describes the argument as a misleading "intuition pump" which "depends, illicitly, on your imagining too simple a case, an irrelevant case". | sep-chinese-room: Read via the live entry; the passages used here were checked against the downloaded HTML. Records the same Hayes remark, sets out the standing split between defenders of the systems and virtual-mind replies (Block, Chalmers, Hofstadter, Dennett, Cole, Minsky, Sloman, Maudlin) and defenders of Searle's conclusion (Harnad, Penrose), and states in its 2024 revision that recent large language model advances have not resolved the debate.

claim_text_en: In 1949 the psychologist Bertram Forer gave 39 students a personality questionnaire, and a week later handed each of them a character sketch supposedly derived from their own answers. Every sketch was identical: thirteen statements assembled largely from a newsstand astrology book. Asked how well the sketch revealed their basic personality, on a scale of 0 to 5, the class averaged 4.26; sixteen of 39 called it a perfect 5 and only five rated it below 4. Later studies repeated the trick many times over: most people rate a vague, general sketch as a good or excellent description of themselves.
claim_text_pl: W 1949 roku psycholog Bertram Forer dał 39 studentom kwestionariusz osobowości, a tydzień później wręczył każdemu z nich portret charakteru rzekomo wyprowadzony z ich własnych odpowiedzi. Każdy portret był identyczny: trzynaście stwierdzeń zebranych w dużej mierze z kioskowej książki astrologicznej. Zapytani, jak dobrze portret oddaje ich podstawową osobowość, w skali od 0 do 5, wystawili średnią 4,26; szesnaścioro z 39 nazwało go idealną piątką, a tylko pięcioro oceniło poniżej 4. Późniejsze badania powtórzyły tę sztuczkę wielokrotnie: większość ludzi ocenia mglisty, ogólny portret jako dobry albo doskonały opis samych siebie.
support_notes_en: forer-1949-personal-validation: Full text read (mirror PDF). Reports the 39-student Diagnostic Interest Blank procedure, the identical 13-statement sketch (footnote 3: 'These statements came largely from a newsstand astrology book'), the 0 (poor) to 5 (perfect) rating instructions, and Table 1's sketch-rating distribution (2: one student, 3: four, 4: eighteen, 5: sixteen; N=39). The paper prints the distribution, not the mean; 166/39 = 4.26. It also reports only one DIB rating below 4 and five sketch ratings below 4. | dickson-kelly-1985-barnum-review: Full text read (mirror PDF). Page 368 states the mean accuracy rating in Forer's study 'was 4.3', that nobody rated the profile below 2 and only 5 subjects below 4, and that the bulk of later researchers using Forer-style methods arrived at the same conclusion: most subjects rate the general Barnum profile as a good or excellent description of their own personalities.

claim_text_en: Forer named the underlying error the fallacy of personal validation: the feeling that a description fits you is no evidence that the method behind it works. The label that stuck came in 1956, when Paul Meehl proposed the term Barnum effect, borrowing his colleague Donald G. Paterson's phrase for personality description after the manner of P. T. Barnum — the showman whose formula was to have a little something for everybody.
claim_text_pl: Forer nazwał leżącą u podłoża pomyłkę błędem osobistej walidacji: poczucie, że opis do ciebie pasuje, nie jest żadnym dowodem, że stojąca za nim metoda działa. Etykieta, która się przyjęła, pojawiła się w 1956 roku, gdy Paul Meehl zaproponował termin efekt Barnuma, pożyczając od swojego kolegi Donalda G. Patersona określenie opisu osobowości na sposób P. T. Barnuma — showmana, którego receptą było mieć po trochu coś dla każdego.
support_notes_en: meehl-1956-good-cookbook: Barnum passage read via a text-rendered copy of the University of Minnesota archive PDF. Meehl writes 'I suggest — and I am quite serious — that we adopt the phrase Barnum effect' for pseudo-successful clinical procedures whose descriptions fit 'largely or wholly by virtue of their triviality', and credits 'my colleague Donald G. Paterson', who calls it 'personality description after the manner of P. T. Barnum'. American Psychologist, 1956, 11, 263-272. | dickson-kelly-1985-barnum-review: Full text read. Page 367 defines the Barnum effect as 'the tendency for people to accept vague, ambiguous, and general statements as descriptive of their unique personalities', notes the name is after P. T. Barnum, 'a famous circus owner whose formula for success was always to have a little something for everybody', and page 368 restates Forer's caution that personal validation cannot affirm the validity of the assessment device.

claim_text_en: In Ray Hyman's classic analysis, a reading is a collaboration the sitter does not know they have joined. Trying to make sense of the reader's statements, the client searches their own life for matches, supplies specifics, and often does most of the talking; Hyman describes a tea-leaf reading in which the client spent three quarters of the session speaking, then praised the reader for telling her what she had in fact said herself. The reader can be as taken in as the sitter: Hyman read palms in his teens and became a believer, until he tried giving readings opposite to what the lines indicated and found them received just as well.
claim_text_pl: W klasycznej analizie Raya Hymana odczyt jest współpracą, do której klient nie wie, że przystąpił. Próbując nadać sens stwierdzeniom osoby prowadzącej odczyt, klient przeszukuje własne życie w poszukiwaniu dopasowań, dostarcza szczegółów i często sam mówi najwięcej; Hyman opisuje odczyt z fusów herbaty, w którym klientka przegadała trzy czwarte sesji, po czym pochwaliła osobę prowadzącą odczyt za to, że powiedziała jej to, co w rzeczywistości powiedziała ona sama. Prowadzący odczyt może być nabrany tak samo jak klient: Hyman jako nastolatek wróżył z dłoni i sam uwierzył, aż spróbował dawać odczyty przeciwne do tego, co wskazywały linie, i odkrył, że są przyjmowane równie dobrze.
support_notes_en: hyman-1977-cold-reading: Full text read (mirror PDF of the 1977 Zetetic article). States that the client, made an active participant, will 'strive to fit your generalities to his specific life occurrences' and later recall the reading 'in terms of specifics'; recounts the observed tea-leaf reading in which the client 'actually spent 75 percent of the total time talking' yet insisted she had not uttered a single word; and gives Hyman's first-person account of believing in palmistry until reversed readings, suggested by mentalist Stanley Saks, proved 'just as successful as ever'. Cited here as analysis and case description, not as a manual.

claim_text_en: What moves the ratings is not the sketch but the staging around it. Being told a profile was written specifically for you raises acceptance — a replicated finding — and favourably worded sketches are accepted more readily than unfavourable ones. Personalised ritual works too: in one series, the same fake sketch was rated about 3.2 out of 5 when presented as generally true of all people, 3.76 when a supposed astrologer was given the sitter's year and month of birth, and 4.98 when the astrologer was also given the day of birth.
claim_text_pl: Ocenami porusza nie sam portret, lecz inscenizacja wokół niego. Usłyszenie, że profil napisano specjalnie dla ciebie, podnosi jego akceptację — to wynik zreplikowany — a portrety sformułowane pochlebnie przyjmowane są chętniej niż niepochlebne. Spersonalizowany rytuał też działa: w jednej serii ten sam spreparowany portret oceniano na około 3,2 na 5, gdy przedstawiano go jako ogólnie prawdziwy dla wszystkich ludzi, na 3,76, gdy rzekomemu astrologowi podano rok i miesiąc urodzenia klienta, i na 4,98, gdy astrolog dostał również dzień urodzenia.
support_notes_en: dickson-kelly-1985-barnum-review: Full text read. Conclusion propositions 2 and 4: 'One can increase acceptance of a Barnum profile by labelling the profile "for you"' (Snyder & Larson 1972, subsequently replicated) and 'Favorable interpretations are more readily accepted' (Sundberg 1955, subsequently replicated); the review also documents the replications and the exceptions. | hyman-1977-cold-reading: Full text read. Reports C. R. Snyder's University of Kansas series (via Snyder & Shenkel 1975): the fake sketch presented as 'generally true for all people' rated about 3.2; supplying the mythical astrologer with year and month of birth raised the mean to 3.76; year, month and day of birth raised it to 4.98. Secondary reporting of Snyder's experiments — the primary papers were not opened.

claim_text_en: In 2002 the US Federal Trade Commission settled with the Florida companies behind the Miss Cleo psychic hotline, charged with deceptive advertising, billing and collection practices — readings promoted as free that ran up pay-per-call charges. The settlement halted collections, forgave an estimated 500 million dollars in outstanding consumer charges, required a further 5 million, and barred the promoters from the pay-per-call business.
claim_text_pl: W 2002 roku amerykańska Federalna Komisja Handlu zawarła ugodę z florydzkimi firmami stojącymi za jasnowidzką infolinią Miss Cleo, oskarżonymi o zwodnicze praktyki reklamowe, rozliczeniowe i windykacyjne — odczyty reklamowane jako darmowe nabijały opłaty za połączenia o podwyższonej płatności. Ugoda wstrzymała windykację, umorzyła szacowane na 500 milionów dolarów nierozliczone obciążenia konsumentów, nakazała zapłatę kolejnych 5 milionów i zakazała promotorom działalności na numerach o podwyższonej opłacie.
support_notes_en: ftc-2002-miss-cleo-settlement: Press release text read via a text-rendering proxy (ftc.gov returned 403 to direct fetching). Dated November 14, 2002; names Access Resource Services, Inc. and Psychic Readers Network, Inc. with officers Steven L. Feder and Peter Stolz; alleges misrepresentation that consumers would receive readings at no charge, Pay-Per-Call Rule violations and collection threats; settlement forgives approximately $500 million in outstanding consumer charges, requires a $5 million payment, halts collections and bans the defendants from pay-per-call operations.

claim_text_en: Accepting a Barnum sketch is not proof of gullibility — the review literature says so directly: people accept many of the statements because the statements genuinely do fit most of us, and because a listener has nothing else to compare them against. When experimenters ask directly, subjects can tell the difference between a sketch being accurate and being unique to them; whether anyone thinks to draw that distinction unprompted, mid-reading, is exactly what remains in doubt.
claim_text_pl: Przyjęcie portretu Barnuma nie jest dowodem łatwowierności — literatura przeglądowa mówi to wprost: ludzie akceptują wiele z tych stwierdzeń, bo stwierdzenia te naprawdę pasują do większości z nas i bo słuchacz nie ma ich z czym porównać. Kiedy eksperymentatorzy pytają wprost, badani potrafią odróżnić trafność portretu od jego wyjątkowości akurat dla nich; czy komukolwiek przyjdzie do głowy zrobić to rozróżnienie bez podpowiedzi, w trakcie odczytu, pozostaje właśnie pod znakiem zapytania.
support_notes_en: dickson-kelly-1985-barnum-review: Full text read. Page 369: the assumption that accepting Barnum statements shows people 'are therefore gullible' is 'surely... incorrect' — 'People accept many Barnum statements because they do fit, and because they do not have anything else with which to compare them.' Conclusion proposition 3: subjects can distinguish accuracy from uniqueness 'when they are specifically asked to do so. It is unclear whether or not subjects do so when not directly asked.' The Greene versus Snyder et al. discrepancy on this point is discussed as a measurement conflict.

claim_text_en: The Barnum-effect literature is broad but bounded: most studies were run on university students rating written profiles in classrooms, the effect of assessment type was inconsistent and methodologically contested, and the 1985 reviewers themselves called for work with the general public and in one-to-one clinical settings — closer to a paid reading's situation — where the effect had barely been tested.
claim_text_pl: Literatura o efekcie Barnuma jest szeroka, ale ograniczona: większość badań przeprowadzono na studentach oceniających pisemne profile w salach wykładowych, wpływ rodzaju narzędzia diagnostycznego bywał niespójny i metodologicznie kwestionowany, a autorzy przeglądu z 1985 roku sami wzywali do badań na ogólnej populacji i w warunkach klinicznych jeden na jednego — bliższych sytuacji płatnego odczytu — gdzie efekt był ledwie sprawdzony.
support_notes_en: dickson-kelly-1985-barnum-review: Full text read. Suggestions for Future Research: 'the majority of studies have been conducted with university students' and research 'might examine responses to Barnum profiles with the general public'; 'Barnum research has not adequately addressed the importance of the actual clinical situation'; evidence on assessment devices 'has been inconsistent and subject to methodological criticism (Weinberger, 1980)'. The same section names cold reading effects, selective memory and hindsight bias as understudied contributors, citing Hyman.

claim_text_en: design tricks that nudge you into buying more or sharing more than you meant to are common enough that you have almost certainly met them: fake urgency timers, "only 2 left!" messages, or subscriptions that are easy to start and hard to stop. When researchers crawled about 11,000 shopping websites, they found 1,818 instances of these "dark patterns" on roughly 11% of the sites, and the more popular a site was, the more likely it was to use them.
claim_text_pl: sztuczki projektowe, które popychają cię do kupowania albo udostępniania więcej, niż zamierzasz, są na tyle powszechne, że niemal na pewno zdarzyło ci się już je spotkać: fałszywe zegary odliczające, komunikaty „zostały tylko 2 sztuki!” albo subskrypcje, które łatwo zacząć i trudno zakończyć. Kiedy badacze przeczesali automatycznie około 11 000 sklepów internetowych, znaleźli 1818 wystąpień tych „dark patterns” na mniej więcej 11% witryn, a im popularniejsza była witryna, tym większa była szansa, że ich używa.
support_notes_en: mathur-2019-dark-patterns-at-scale: Abstract (read in full via arXiv) states: ~53K product pages from ~11K shopping websites analyzed; 1,818 dark pattern instances discovered, representing 15 types and 7 broader categories; 183 websites engaged in outright deceptive practices; 22 third-party entities offer dark patterns as a turnkey solution. | princeton-dark-patterns-project: Project page (read) gives the 11.1% figure — approximately 11.1% of the ~11K shopping websites (1,254 sites) contained at least one dark pattern — and states that more popular websites (by Alexa ranking) were more likely to feature dark patterns; also lists per-category instance counts and the 22 third-party vendors (e.g., Beeketing on 406 sites).

claim_text_en: The term "dark patterns" was introduced in 2010 by UX specialist Harry Brignull, who began cataloguing them at darkpatterns.org (now renamed deceptive.design, with the preferred term "deceptive patterns"). Researchers later sorted practitioner-collected examples into five recurring strategies you can learn to spot: nagging (repeated interruptions), obstruction (making a task needlessly hard, like cancelling), sneaking (hiding relevant information or costs), interface interference (visually privileging the choice the company wants), and forced action (making you do something extra to get what you came for).
claim_text_pl: Termin „dark patterns” wprowadził w 2010 roku specjalista od UX Harry Brignull, który zaczął je katalogować na darkpatterns.org (dziś przemianowanej na deceptive.design, z preferowanym terminem „deceptive patterns”). Badacze uporządkowali później przykłady zebrane przez praktyków w pięć powracających strategii, których można nauczyć się rozpoznawać: nagabywanie (powtarzane przerywanie), utrudnianie (niepotrzebne komplikowanie zadania, na przykład rezygnacji), przemycanie (ukrywanie istotnych informacji albo kosztów), zakłócanie interfejsu (wizualne uprzywilejowanie wyboru, na którym zależy firmie) i wymuszone działanie (zmuszanie cię do zrobienia czegoś dodatkowego, żeby dostać to, po co przychodzisz).
support_notes_en: brignull-deceptive-design-about: Page (read) confirms the site was launched in 2010 by Harry Brignull to address manipulative, deceptive and coercive design patterns, explains the rename from darkpatterns.org to deceptive.design, and notes the terminology has been adopted in laws including the EU DSA and California's CPRA. | gray-2018-dark-patterns-side-ux: Official abstract (read in full via Semantic Scholar API) describes assembling a corpus of practitioner-identified dark patterns and content-analyzing them; the authors' UXP2 lab site (darkpatterns.uxp2.com, also read) names and defines the five resulting strategies: nagging, obstruction, sneaking, interface interference, forced action, and states the work builds on Brignull's.

claim_text_en: These designs are not just irritating — controlled experiments show they measurably change what people do. In a randomized experiment with a census-weighted US sample of about 1,900 adults, only 11.3% of a control group accepted a dubious paid identity-theft-protection service, versus 25.8% exposed to mild dark patterns and 41.9% exposed to aggressive ones; hiding information and trick questions were among the most effective single techniques, and less-educated participants were significantly more susceptible to the mild versions.
claim_text_pl: Te rozwiązania nie tylko irytują — kontrolowane eksperymenty pokazują, że w mierzalny sposób zmieniają to, co ludzie robią. W eksperymencie z losowym przydziałem, na amerykańskiej próbie około 1900 dorosłych ważonej według danych spisu powszechnego, tylko 11,3% grupy kontrolnej przyjęło wątpliwą płatną usługę ochrony przed kradzieżą tożsamości, wobec 25,8% wśród osób wystawionych na łagodne dark patterns i 41,9% wśród wystawionych na agresywne; ukrywanie informacji i podchwytliwe pytania należały do najskuteczniejszych pojedynczych technik, a osoby z niższym wykształceniem były istotnie bardziej podatne na łagodne wersje.
support_notes_en: luguri-strahilevitz-2021-shining-light: Open-access article page (read) reports Study 1 (n=1,963, census-weighted): acceptance 11.3% control vs 25.8% mild vs 41.9% aggressive dark patterns; Study 2 (n=3,777) isolating techniques: hidden information roughly doubled acceptance (30.1% vs 14.8%), trick questions raised it from 19.2% to 33.4%; less-educated participants were significantly more susceptible to mild dark patterns controlling for income and demographics.

claim_text_en: Regulators on both sides of the Atlantic now treat many of these designs as unlawful rather than merely annoying. A 2022 US Federal Trade Commission staff report, "Bringing Dark Patterns to Light," details four common tactics — ads disguised as independent content, hard-to-cancel subscriptions, buried terms and junk fees, and tricks that steer people into giving up personal data — and the EU's Digital Services Act (Article 25) prohibits online platforms from designing interfaces that deceive or manipulate users or materially distort their ability to make free and informed decisions.
claim_text_pl: Regulatorzy po obu stronach Atlantyku traktują dziś wiele z tych rozwiązań projektowych jako bezprawne, a nie tylko uciążliwe. Raport służb amerykańskiej Federalnej Komisji Handlu z 2022 roku, „Bringing Dark Patterns to Light”, opisuje szczegółowo cztery częste taktyki — reklamy przebrane za niezależne treści, subskrypcje trudne do anulowania, zakopane warunki i śmieciowe opłaty oraz sztuczki nakłaniające ludzi do oddania danych osobowych — a unijny akt o usługach cyfrowych (DSA, art. 25) zakazuje platformom internetowym projektowania interfejsów, które wprowadzają użytkowników w błąd, manipulują nimi albo w istotny sposób zaburzają ich zdolność do podejmowania wolnych i świadomych decyzji.
support_notes_en: ftc-2022-dark-patterns-report: Full press release text (retrieved and read) names the four tactic categories exactly as drafted (disguised ads/misleading consumers; difficult-to-cancel subscriptions; buried key terms and junk fees; tricking consumers into sharing data), cites example enforcement cases (ABCmouse, LendingClub, Vizio), notes the 5-0 Commission vote, and states the FTC's commitment to enforcement. | eu-dsa-article-25: Article 25(1) text (read via full-text mirror eu-digital-services-act.com after the EUR-Lex page proved too long to parse): providers of online platforms shall not design, organise or operate their online interfaces in a way that deceives or manipulates recipients or otherwise materially distorts or impairs their ability to make free and informed decisions.

claim_text_en: None of this means every persuasive design is manipulation, or that these tricks work reliably on everyone. Researchers themselves note the umbrella term lumps together ethically quite different practices, prevalence figures depend heavily on the definitions and detection methods used, and experiments find that heavy-handed dark patterns can backfire — in one study the aggressive versions provoked visible anger and far more people simply quitting (65 dropouts versus 9 in the mild condition), which is partly why the subtler patterns are considered the more insidious problem.
claim_text_pl: Nic z tego nie znaczy, że każdy perswazyjny projekt jest manipulacją ani że te sztuczki działają niezawodnie na każdego. Sami badacze zauważają, że ten termin-parasol wrzuca do jednego worka praktyki etycznie bardzo różne, że dane o rozpowszechnieniu silnie zależą od przyjętych definicji i metod wykrywania, a eksperymenty pokazują, że nachalne dark patterns potrafią przynieść odwrotny skutek — w jednym badaniu agresywne wersje wywołały widoczną złość i znacznie więcej rezygnacji z udziału (65 osób, które przerwały, wobec 9 w warunku łagodnym), co jest po części powodem, dla którego to subtelniejsze wzorce uchodzą za bardziej podstępny problem.
support_notes_en: gray-2018-conflation-note: Official abstract (read) states their content analysis "revealed a wide range of ethical issues raised by practitioners that were frequently conflated under the umbrella term of dark patterns" — direct support for the point that the label covers ethically heterogeneous practices. | luguri-strahilevitz-2021-backlash: Article page (read) reports that aggressive dark patterns generated substantial backlash — increased frustration and 65 dropouts versus 9 in the mild condition — while mild dark patterns achieved large conversion gains without triggering comparable emotional backlash, supporting both the 'can backfire' and 'subtle patterns are the harder problem' points.

claim_text_en: In the experiment this station restages, thirty-six students heard six lists of twelve words, each list built entirely from the leading associates of one word that was never read out, and then wrote down everything they could remember. The missing word came back on 40 per cent of the lists — about as often as words that genuinely had been read to them from the middle of the list.
claim_text_pl: W eksperymencie, który odtwarza to stanowisko, trzydziestu sześciu studentów wysłuchało sześciu list po dwanaście słów, z których każda była zbudowana wyłącznie z czołowych skojarzeń jednego słowa, którego nigdy nie przeczytano na głos, a potem zapisało wszystko, co udało im się zapamiętać. Brakujące słowo wracało w 40 procentach list — mniej więcej tak często jak słowa, które naprawdę im przeczytano, ze środka listy.
support_notes_en: roediger-mcdermott-1995: Experiment 1, pp. 804-805: 36 Rice University undergraduates; six lists taken from Deese (1959) — chair, mountain, needle, rough, sleep and sweet — each the first 12 associates from the Russell and Jenkins (1954) norms, read aloud at about 1 word per 1.5 s. The paper also records that "in a few instances, we replaced 1 of the first 12 associates with a word that seemed, in our judgment, more likely to elicit the critical word" (p. 805), so "built entirely from the leading associates" holds exactly for the chair list printed on that page and approximately for the other five. Figure 1 caption: "probability of recall of the studied words was .65, and probability of recall of the critical nonpresented item was .40", and the text states the critical item "was recalled with a probability of .40, or with about the same probability as items that had been presented in the middle of the list". | gallo-2010-drm-review: Abstract characterises the DRM effect as an established "associative memory illusion, whereby people falsely remember words that were not presented" that has "broadly influenced basic theories of memory in cognitive psychology and neuroscience" over fifteen years of research — supporting the "replicated, not a one-off" half of the grade rather than the specific 40 per cent figure.

claim_text_en: The trick is older than the paper that made it famous. In 1959 James Deese built thirty-six lists, each one the twelve primary associates of a word he never read aloud, and found that the chance of a particular word intruding into recall was predicted by how strongly the list pointed at it — a correlation of .87 between intrusion probability and associative strength. His report then sat almost unread: Roediger and McDermott counted fourteen citations in total, and only one since 1983, before they picked it up thirty-six years later.
claim_text_pl: Sztuczka jest starsza niż praca, która ją rozsławiła. W 1959 roku James Deese zbudował trzydzieści sześć list, każdą z dwunastu pierwszych skojarzeń słowa, którego nigdy nie czytał na głos, i stwierdził, że szansę na to, iż dane słowo wtrąci się do odtwarzania, da się przewidzieć na podstawie tego, jak mocno lista w nie celuje — korelacja 0,87 między prawdopodobieństwem intruzji a siłą skojarzenia. Jego doniesienie leżało potem niemal nieczytane: Roediger i McDermott naliczyli w sumie czternaście cytowań, z czego tylko jedno od 1983 roku, zanim trzydzieści sześć lat później sami po nie sięgnęli.
support_notes_en: roediger-mcdermott-1995: p. 804: "he developed 36 lists, 12 words per list. Each list was composed of the 12 primary associates of a critical (nonpresented) word"; "Deese obtained a correlation of .87 between the probability of an intrusion in recall (from one group of subjects) and the probability of occurrence of the word as an associate to members of the list (from a different group)"; and "since the Social Science Citation Index began publication in 1969, the article has been cited only 14 times, and only once since 1983". The 36-year gap is 1959 to 1995. | deese-1959: The primary publication being described. Not consulted directly: the PubMed record confirms author, title, journal, volume and pagination but carries no abstract, and no full text was reachable, so every detail above is taken from Roediger and McDermott's account of it rather than from Deese himself.

claim_text_en: On a recognition test the illusion is sharper than in recall. In Roediger and McDermott's first experiment the false-alarm rate for the missing word was .84, against a hit rate of .86 for words that had actually been studied, while unrelated words drew false alarms only 2 per cent of the time. Asked to rate their confidence on a four-point scale, subjects picked the top point — sure it was old — for the missing word 58 per cent of the time.
claim_text_pl: W teście rozpoznawania złudzenie jest ostrzejsze niż w swobodnym odtwarzaniu. W pierwszym eksperymencie Roedigera i McDermott odsetek fałszywych alarmów dla brakującego słowa wyniósł 0,84, przy odsetku trafień 0,86 dla słów, które naprawdę były na liście, podczas gdy słowa niepowiązane wywoływały fałszywe alarmy tylko w 2 procentach przypadków. Poproszeni o ocenę pewności na czteropunktowej skali, badani wybierali najwyższy punkt — pewność, że słowo było na liście — dla brakującego słowa w 58 procentach przypadków.
support_notes_en: roediger-mcdermott-1995: Experiment 1 Recognition, p. 806 and Table 1: "the hit rate was 86% and the false-alarm rate for the standard type of unrelated lures was only 2%"; "the false-alarm rate for the critical nonstudied lures (.84) approached the hit rate (.86), t(35) < 1". Table 1 gives the proportion of items given a rating of 4 (sure old): studied .75, critical lure .58, weakly related lure .04, unrelated lure .00. | ost-2013-drm-misinformation: Independent replication of the recognition effect in a different laboratory and country: 120 University of Portsmouth undergraduates showed 68 per cent false recognition of critical lures against 3 per cent for new items, F(2,238) = 621.13, p < .001 — a smaller lure rate than Roediger and McDermott's, which is why the claim quotes their figures as theirs rather than as a universal constant.

claim_text_en: In a second experiment with twenty-four fifteen-word lists, false recall rose to 55 per cent, and the experimenters added a question borrowed from Tulving: for every word you call old, say whether you actually remember its presentation or merely know it was there. Of the never-presented words that people called old after studying and then recalling a list, 72 per cent were judged remembered rather than known.
claim_text_pl: W drugim eksperymencie, z dwudziestoma czterema listami po piętnaście słów, fałszywe odtworzenia wzrosły do 55 procent, a eksperymentatorzy dołożyli pytanie zapożyczone od Tulvinga: przy każdym słowie uznanym za widziane wcześniej powiedz, czy naprawdę pamiętasz jego prezentację, czy tylko wiesz, że tam było. Spośród nigdy nieprezentowanych słów, które ludzie uznali za widziane wcześniej po przeczytaniu listy i jej odtworzeniu, 72 procent oceniono jako pamiętane, a nie jako wiedziane.
support_notes_en: roediger-mcdermott-1995: Experiment 2, pp. 807-808: 30 subjects, 24 lists of 15 associates from Russell and Jenkins (1954) presented by tape at a 1.5-s rate. Results: "Subjects recalled the critical nonpresented word on 55% of the lists". Table 2 and text: in the study + recall condition the critical lure was called old .81 of the time, of which remember judgments were .58 — "with remember judgments being made 72% of the time (i.e., .58 divided by .81 times 100) for words that had never been presented". The remember-know procedure is attributed in the paper to Tulving (1985). Graded supported_with_limits rather than convergent_or_replicated: unlike the recall and recognition claims above, no independent replication of the remember/know split was opened for this entry, so the warrant is one experiment (n = 30) in the constituting paper.

claim_text_en: Whether this illusion indexes anything about false memory outside the word list is contested. Ost and colleagues gave 120 people a standard misinformation experiment — CCTV footage followed by misleading information about it — and a DRM test as an apparently unrelated filler; both effects came out robustly, and the correlations between them averaged r = -.01, with reliability and statistical power ruled out as explanations. Reviewers of the paradigm point the other way, linking individual differences in this illusion to false autobiographical memories and even to fantastic beliefs, and argue that the question can only be settled by isolating the several distinct processes that produce even the simplest false memory.
claim_text_pl: To, czy to złudzenie mówi cokolwiek o fałszywej pamięci poza listą słów, jest sporne. Ost i współpracownicy dali 120 osobom standardowy eksperyment z dezinformacją — nagranie z monitoringu, a po nim mylące informacje na jego temat — oraz test DRM jako pozornie niezwiązane zadanie wypełniające; oba efekty wyszły mocno, a korelacje między nimi wyniosły średnio r = -0,01, przy czym rzetelność i moc statystyczną wykluczono jako wyjaśnienia. Autorzy przeglądów tego paradygmatu wskazują w drugą stronę: wiążą różnice indywidualne w tym złudzeniu z fałszywymi wspomnieniami autobiograficznymi, a nawet z fantastycznymi przekonaniami, i twierdzą, że pytanie da się rozstrzygnąć tylko przez wyodrębnienie kilku różnych procesów, które wytwarzają nawet najprostsze fałszywe wspomnienie.
support_notes_en: ost-2013-drm-misinformation: Abstract and results: 120 participants watched CCTV footage, received misleading post-event information, completed free recall and recognition tests, and did a DRM test "as an ostensibly unrelated filler task"; "Despite obtaining robust misinformation and DRM effects, there were no correlations between a broad range of misinformation and DRM effect measures (mean r = -.01). This was not due to reliability issues with our measures or a lack of power." | gallo-2010-drm-review: Abstract supplies the opposing side: "Some applicability is evident from research linking individual differences in the DRM illusion to false autobiographical memories (e.g., misremembering public events) and fantastic autobiographical beliefs (e.g., memories from past lives). But which aspects generalize?" — and argues that "multiple and often opposing psychological processes cause even the most basic false memories", so isolating component processes is required to answer the question.

claim_text_en: When Stadler, Roediger and McDermott collected normative data for thirty-six of these lists, the spread was enormous: 60 per cent or more of subjects falsely recalled window and sleep after the matching lists, with false recognition above 80 per cent, while the list built from king produced 10 per cent false recall and 27 per cent false recognition.
claim_text_pl: Kiedy Stadler, Roediger i McDermott zebrali dane normalizacyjne dla trzydziestu sześciu takich list, rozrzut okazał się ogromny: 60 procent badanych lub więcej fałszywie odtwarzało słowa window i sleep po odpowiadających im listach, przy fałszywym rozpoznaniu powyżej 80 procent, podczas gdy lista zbudowana wokół słowa king dała 10 procent fałszywych odtworzeń i 27 procent fałszywych rozpoznań.
support_notes_en: stadler-1999-drm-norms: Abstract: "We tested false recall and false recognition for critical targets from 36 lists. Despite the fact that all lists were constructed to produce false remembering, the diversity in their effectiveness was large--60% or more of subjects falsely recalled window and sleep following the appropriate lists, and false recognition for these items was greater than 80%. However, the list generated from king led to 10% false recall and 27% false recognition."

claim_text_en: Being warned in advance does not simply switch the illusion off, and how much it helps depends on the person and on practice. Given an explicit warning before study and five study-test trials on the same list, young adults virtually eliminated false recall by the second trial; older adults used the warning to cut false recall on the first trial and then could not reduce it any further across the remaining four, which the authors read as a breakdown in spontaneous, self-initiated source monitoring rather than an inability to follow instructions.
claim_text_pl: Uprzedzenie z góry nie wyłącza po prostu złudzenia, a to, ile daje, zależy od osoby i od wprawy. Przy wyraźnym ostrzeżeniu przed uczeniem się i pięciu próbach uczenie–test na tej samej liście młodzi dorośli praktycznie zlikwidowali fałszywe odtworzenia już w drugiej próbie; starsi dorośli wykorzystali ostrzeżenie, żeby obniżyć fałszywe odtworzenia w pierwszej próbie, a potem nie potrafili ich zmniejszyć już ani trochę przez pozostałe cztery, co autorzy odczytują jako załamanie spontanicznego, samodzielnie inicjowanego monitorowania źródła, a nie jako niezdolność do stosowania się do instrukcji.
support_notes_en: watson-mcdermott-balota-2004: Abstract: half of each age group "were given an explicit warning about the DRM paradigm prior to encoding and were asked to attempt to avoid recalling any associated but nonpresented words"; "When a warning about false recall was provided, young adults virtually eliminated false recall by the second trial. Even though old adults also used warnings to reduce false recall on Trial 1, they were still unable to decrease false memories across the remaining four study-test trials"; the authors conclude that old adults "have a breakdown in spontaneous, self-initiated source monitoring". Graded supported_with_limits because this is a single study of one repeated list, and the wider warning literature is itself mixed.

claim_text_en: The shape was pinned down in 1966, when Jonathan Freedman and Scott Fraser sent researchers around Palo Alto to ask residents for something tiny — display a three-inch "Be a safe driver" sign, or sign a petition — and then, about two weeks later and through a different person, asked them to let a large, poorly lettered "Drive Carefully" sign be planted on their front lawn. Of those asked only the large question, 16.7% agreed; among those who had been asked something small first, the lowest agreement in any condition was over 45%, and it reached 76% where the two requests concerned the same cause and the same kind of act.
claim_text_pl: Kształt tego wzorca uchwycono w 1966 roku, kiedy Jonathan Freedman i Scott Fraser wysłali badaczy po Palo Alto, żeby prosili mieszkańców o coś drobnego — o wystawienie trzycalowej tabliczki „Bądź bezpiecznym kierowcą” albo o podpis pod petycją — a potem, jakieś dwa tygodnie później i przez inną osobę, poprosili ich o zgodę na wkopanie na frontowym trawniku dużej, kiepsko wymalowanej tablicy „Jedź ostrożnie”. Spośród tych, którym zadano tylko to duże pytanie, zgodziło się 16,7%; wśród tych, których wcześniej poproszono o coś małego, najniższy odsetek zgód w którymkolwiek z warunków przekroczył 45%, a sięgnął 76% tam, gdzie obie prośby dotyczyły tej samej sprawy i tego samego rodzaju czynu.
support_notes_en: freedman-fraser-1966: Full text read (scanned JPSP offprint). Experiment II method, pp. 200-201: 114 women and 13 men in Palo Alto; the small sign was "3 inches square", said "Be a safe driver", was "on thin paper without a gummed backing" and looked "rather amateurish"; the alternative first request was a petition to California's US Senators. The second contact came "about 2 weeks after the initial one", always from the other of two experimenters, who was blind to condition, and asked for a large "Drive Carefully" sign, "rather poorly lettered", shown in a photograph in which it obscured the front of a house. Table 2 (p. 201) gives One-Contact 16.7 (N=24), Similar issue/Similar task 76.0 (N=25), Similar/Different 47.8 (N=23), Different/Similar 47.6 (N=21), Different/Different 47.4 (N=19); the Results text states "over 45% being the lowest degree of compliance for any experimental condition".

claim_text_en: Freedman and Fraser's own account was about self-image: agreeing to the first request, they suggested, can change how you see yourself — you become, in your own eyes, "the kind of person who does this sort of thing", someone who agrees to strangers' requests and cooperates with good causes. They were careful to add that their studies offered no data with which to support or refute any of the possible explanations.
claim_text_pl: Wyjaśnienie samych Freedmana i Frasera dotyczyło obrazu siebie: zgoda na pierwszą prośbę — jak sugerowali — może zmienić to, jak siebie widzisz; stajesz się we własnych oczach „kimś, kto robi takie rzeczy”, kto przystaje na prośby nieznajomych i współpracuje w dobrych sprawach. Starannie zastrzegli przy tym, że ich badania nie dostarczają żadnych danych, którymi dałoby się poprzeć albo obalić którekolwiek z możliwych wyjaśnień.
support_notes_en: freedman-fraser-1966: Discussion, pp. 201-202, read in full. The authors propose that once a person has agreed to a request "his attitude may change" and that he may become, in his own eyes, "the kind of person who does this sort of thing, who agrees to requests made by strangers, who takes action on things he believes in, who cooperates with good causes". The following paragraph states that "the present studies offer no additional data with which to support or refute any of the possible explanations of the effect" and that the proposals "remain simply descriptions of mechanisms which might produce" it.

claim_text_en: Reviewing the literature that followed, Jerry Burger identified six processes a foot-in-the-door manipulation can set going — self-perception, psychological reactance, conformity, consistency, attributions and commitment — and argued that their combined effects account not only for the successful demonstrations but for the studies in which the technique did nothing, or reduced compliance instead.
claim_text_pl: Przeglądając literaturę, która narosła później, Jerry Burger wskazał sześć procesów, jakie manipulacja typu stopa w drzwiach potrafi uruchomić — samopostrzeganie, reaktancję psychologiczną, konformizm, konsekwencję, atrybucje i zaangażowanie — i dowodził, że ich łączne działanie tłumaczy nie tylko udane demonstracje, ale i te badania, w których technika nie dała nic albo wręcz zmniejszyła uległość.
support_notes_en: burger-1999-fitd: Abstract read in full via the Europe PMC record; the review itself is paywalled. The abstract names exactly these six processes — "self-perception, psychological reactance, conformity, consistency, attributions, and commitment" — states that a review of relevant investigations and several meta-analyses support the notion that each can influence compliance in the FITD situation, and argues that their combined effects can account for successful demonstrations "as well as studies in which the technique was ineffective or led to a decrease in compliance". No effect sizes from the body of the review are asserted here, because the body was not opened.

claim_text_en: Pooling 120 experimental groups from the first fifteen years of research, Beaman and colleagues concluded that the phenomenon, though replicable, is weak and not nearly as robust as assumed, and that nearly half of the studies either produced no effect or an effect in the wrong direction.
claim_text_pl: Zsumowawszy 120 grup eksperymentalnych z pierwszych piętnastu lat badań, Beaman i współpracownicy stwierdzili, że zjawisko, choć powtarzalne, jest słabe i wcale nie tak mocne, jak zakładano, oraz że blisko połowa badań dała albo brak efektu, albo efekt w złą stronę.
support_notes_en: beaman-1983: Publisher abstract read in full at SAGE; the article body is paywalled. The abstract states that "A total of 120 experimental groups were examined", that the statistical combinations were "consistent in indicating that the phenomenon, although replicable, is weak and not nearly as robust as assumed", and that "Nearly half of the studies either produced no effects or effects in the wrong direction". It also reports that the common self-perception explanation was found imprecise in leading to clear predictions. | burger-1999-fitd: Corroborating: the abstract of this later review states that the combined processes account for studies in which the technique "was ineffective or led to a decrease in compliance", which is the same two-sided picture the 1983 meta-analysis reports.

claim_text_en: Freedman and Fraser were plain about how narrow their result was: every request in their studies came from an apparently non-profit service organisation, the issues were deliberately uncontroversial, and they wrote that whether the technique would work for selling a product, a political candidate or a dogma remained to be shown. They also reported that in their telephone study, nobody who refused the small request later agreed to the large one.
claim_text_pl: Freedman i Fraser mówili wprost, jak wąski był ich wynik: każda prośba w ich badaniach pochodziła od organizacji sprawiającej wrażenie niedochodowej i działającej w interesie publicznym, tematy były celowo niekontrowersyjne, a oni sami napisali, że dopiero trzeba wykazać, czy technika zadziała przy sprzedawaniu produktu, kandydata politycznego albo doktryny. Odnotowali też, że w ich badaniu telefonicznym nikt, kto odmówił małej prośbie, nie zgodził się później na dużą.
support_notes_en: freedman-fraser-1966: Discussion, p. 202: "In all cases the requests were made by presumably nonprofit service organizations. The issues in the second study were deliberately noncontroversial", set "in strong contrast to campaigns which are designed to sell a particular product, political candidate, or dogma", and "Whether the technique employed in this study would be successful in these other situations remains to be shown." Experiment I Results, p. 197: "none of those who refused the first request later agreed to the large request", with about two thirds of Performance and Agree-Only subjects agreeing to the small one.

claim_text_en: Gamian-Wilk and Dolinski note that the effect size Freedman and Fraser obtained has never been obtained again, and their own direct repetitions of the original experiment found the technique effective in Ukraine but not in Poland in 2003, and statistically insignificant in both countries by 2013, alongside a general drop in compliance over time.
claim_text_pl: Gamian-Wilk i Doliński odnotowują, że wielkości efektu uzyskanej przez Freedmana i Frasera nigdy nie udało się uzyskać ponownie, a ich własne bezpośrednie powtórzenia oryginalnego eksperymentu wykazały, że w 2003 roku technika była skuteczna na Ukrainie, ale nie w Polsce, a do 2013 roku była statystycznie nieistotna w obu krajach — przy ogólnym spadku uległości w czasie.
support_notes_en: gamian-wilk-dolinski-2020: Abstract read in full via the Europe PMC record; the article is paywalled. It states that "the effect sizes reported in meta-analysis studies tend to be low and the effect size obtained by Freedman and Fraser in their studies has never been obtained again"; that the authors ran "a direct replication of the original foot-in-the-door experiment in two time intervals and in two countries"; that "The results indicate a drop of compliance over time"; and that "while in 2003 the foot-in-the-door strategy was effective in Ukraine and ineffective in Poland, in 2013, the effect was insignificant in both Ukraine and Poland". Sample sizes and effect sizes are in the unread body and are not asserted here.

claim_text_en: A meta-analysis by Pascual and Guéguen pooled the studies that pit foot-in-the-door directly against its mirror image, door-in-the-face, in which an outsized request comes first so that a smaller one looks reasonable: across 22 comparisons on each side and roughly 1,600 participants per technique, it found no significant difference in efficiency between the two.
claim_text_pl: Metaanaliza Pascuala i Guéguena zebrała badania, w których stopę w drzwiach zestawiono wprost z jej lustrzanym odbiciem, czyli techniką drzwiami w twarz, w której najpierw pada prośba wygórowana, żeby ta mniejsza wyglądała rozsądnie: na 22 porównaniach po każdej stronie i mniej więcej 1600 uczestnikach na technikę nie znalazła istotnej różnicy w skuteczności między nimi.
support_notes_en: pascual-gueguen-2005: Abstract read in full via the Europe PMC record; the article is paywalled. It states the study "is based on the accumulated studies directly comparing foot-in-the-door (n=22, subjects= 1581) and door-in-the-face (n=22, subjects= 1611) under a similar target request" and that "Analysis indicated no significant differences in efficiency between the paradigms". The gloss on what door-in-the-face is comes from the technique's standard definition, not from a number in this abstract.

claim_text_en: People who have lived through gaslighting usually describe a slow pattern, not one bad conversation: someone close to them repeatedly denies things that happened, treats their reactions as oversensitive or imagined, and over many such moments they begin to doubt their own memory and judgment. Survivors also report that this typically unfolds inside relationships that contain real affection alongside the manipulation, which is part of why the self-doubt takes hold.
claim_text_pl: Osoby, które przeszły przez gaslighting, zwykle opisują powolny wzorzec, a nie jedną złą rozmowę: ktoś bliski wielokrotnie zaprzecza temu, co się wydarzyło, traktuje ich reakcje jako przewrażliwienie albo wymysł, a po wielu takich momentach zaczynają wątpić we własną pamięć i własny osąd. Mówią też, że dzieje się to zazwyczaj w relacjach, w których obok manipulacji jest prawdziwe uczucie — i to po części tłumaczy, dlaczego zwątpienie w siebie tak się zakorzenia.
support_notes_en: abramson-2014: Read pp. 1-3 of the full PDF (via philevents.org mirror). The paper opens with a list of characteristic gaslighter phrases ('You're crazy', 'That never happened', 'You're overreacting'), and states that gaslighting 'almost always involves multiple incidents that take place over long stretches of time', that it induces the sense that one's reactions, perceptions, memories and/or beliefs are 'utterly without grounds', and that it frequently involves isolating the target. This directly supports the 'slow pattern, repeated denial, growing self-doubt' description. | klein-2023: Full abstract read via the Crossref API record. Abstract reports a survey of 65 self-identified gaslighting survivors (ages 18-69, mostly female and heterosexual) and finds gaslighting typically occurred in relationships mixing affectionate and abusive dynamics, with victims experiencing diminished self-perception and interpersonal mistrust. Supports the 'affection alongside manipulation' and 'self-doubt' parts of the claim.

claim_text_en: The name comes from fiction: in Patrick Hamilton's 1938 play Gas Light and its film adaptations (Britain 1940, Hollywood 1944), a husband secretly dims the gas lamps and then denies anything has changed, as part of a campaign to convince his wife she is going mad. The word crossed into medical writing with a 1969 Lancet report, became a therapy-world term in the 1980s, and went fully mainstream in the 2010s–2020s.
claim_text_pl: Nazwa pochodzi z fikcji: w sztuce Patricka Hamiltona Gas Light z 1938 roku i w jej filmowych adaptacjach (Wielka Brytania 1940, Hollywood 1944) mąż po cichu przygasza lampy gazowe, a potem zaprzecza, że cokolwiek się zmieniło, w ramach kampanii mającej przekonać jego żonę, że traci rozum. Do piśmiennictwa medycznego słowo trafiło wraz z doniesieniem opublikowanym w 1969 roku w „Lancecie”, w latach 80. XX wieku stało się terminem środowiska terapeutycznego, a w latach 10. i 20. XXI wieku na dobre weszło do głównego nurtu.
support_notes_en: abramson-2014: Pages 1-2 (read directly) recount the film's plot — Gregory manipulating Paula, the gaslights dimming when he searches the attic, his denials, his aim of having her hospitalized — and state that in the 1980s 'gaslighting' became a term of art in therapeutic practice and has since entered colloquial usage. Supports the film origin and the 1980s therapeutic adoption. | wikipedia-gaslighting: Article (opened and read) documents Patrick Hamilton's 1938 British play Gas Light, the 1940 British and 1944 American film adaptations, the dimming-gaslights plot device, Barton and Whitehead's 1969 Lancet case reports, and Merriam-Webster naming 'gaslighting' its 2022 Word of the Year. Supports the play/film dates and the mainstreaming timeline. | barton-whitehead-1969: This is the primary record for the claim's '1969 Lancet report' element — case reports of people manipulated toward involuntary psychiatric commitment. Citation details (authors, title, journal, volume, pages, DOI, PMID) were verified via the Semantic Scholar API record, but the article text itself was not opened (Elsevier paywall; PubMed page cookie-walled).

claim_text_en: Philosopher Kate Abramson argues that gaslighting differs from ordinary dismissiveness in what it aims at: the manipulation works to make a person feel their reactions are not merely wrong but groundless — "crazy" — so that they stop taking themselves seriously as an independent thinker and judge of reality. On this account the harm is partly epistemic (an attack on someone's standing as a knower), and the tactic often leans on sexist stereotypes that cast women as irrational.
claim_text_pl: Filozofka Kate Abramson twierdzi, że gaslighting różni się od zwykłego lekceważenia tym, do czego zmierza: manipulacja ma sprawić, że ktoś poczuje, iż jego reakcje są nie tylko błędne, ale wręcz bezpodstawne — „szalone” — i przestanie traktować siebie poważnie jako kogoś, kto samodzielnie myśli i samodzielnie ocenia rzeczywistość.
